verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026, from Kennedy Space Center at 6:35 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launch countdown live on April 1... from Kennedy Space Center'; R3: 'leaving Earth on April 1... Liftoff! NASA’s Artemis II rocket... launched at 6:35 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, April 1, 2026 from Launch Complex 39B'; R4: 'Launch date April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC (6:35:12 p.m. EDT)... Launch site Kennedy, LC-39B'; R7: 'lift off from Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 6:35 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact date, location, and time of the successful launch.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'roughly 10-day deep space excursion'; R2: 'return in 10 days'; R3: 'nearly 10-day journey around the moon'; R4: 'Mission duration 9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes... April 1–11, 2026'; R7: '10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe it as a 10-day mission, with precise duration aligning (launch April 1 to splashdown April 10/11).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is not a landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'mission around the moon... does not include [landing]... aim to land astronauts [future]'; R2: 'orbiting the moon... no landing'; R3: 'didn’t touch down on the moon’s surface'; R4: 'Crewed lunar flyby mission... not enter lunar orbit... free-return trajectory'
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state no landing, only flyby/orbit around moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a crewed flyby of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'mission around the moon... loop around Earth before slingshotting around the moon'; R2: 'orbiting the moon'; R3: 'lunar flyby'; R4: 'crewed lunar flyby mission... looping around the far side'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported as crewed lunar flyby in primary sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will feature live views of the astronauts' activities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA will stream the launch... Live coverage... broadcast will track the four-person crew'; R3: Multiple 'livestream', 'live feed', 'NASA's live coverage', views of crew activities, press conferences; R6: 'Live and original programming... livestreams of current space missions'; R7: 'NASA plans to continue broadcasting live views... live views from Orion'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm live streams and broadcasts of crew activities during mission.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will feature views of space from the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'stunning views as the Orion spacecraft... views from a camera on the Orion... Earthset view... images from a camera on the Orion's solar array wing'; R4: 'Earthset Taken from Artemis II... Hello, World photograph taken... from Integrity'
verifications.reasoning: Extensive descriptions of space/Earth/moon views from Orion capsule cameras and windows.
